questions.question: What is the geometric and orbital structure of the transition state during an SN2 displacement on a chiral carbon?

options.label: A
options.text: A tetrahedral intermediate with a pentavalent carbon atom.

options.label: B
options.text: A trigonal bipyramidal arrangement where the central carbon is sp²-like, with the nucleophile and leaving group occupying axial positions at 180°.

options.label: C
options.text: A square planar complex with 90° bond angles.

options.label: D
options.text: A planar carbocation with completely dissociated leaving group.

questions.correct_answer: A trigonal bipyramidal arrangement where the central carbon is sp²-like, with the nucleophile and leaving group occupying axial positions at 180°.
questions.explanation: The nucleophile donates electron density into the σ* anti-bonding orbital directly opposite the leaving group, causing umbrella-like stereoinversion.

questions.question: Why does the bromination of trans-2-butene yield exclusively the meso diastereomer?

options.label: A
options.text: The two bromines add simultaneously to the same face of the alkene.

options.label: B
options.text: Bromine forms a symmetrical bridged bromonium ion; subsequent backside attack by bromide at either carbon occurs with equal probability to produce identical meso enantiomeric faces.

options.label: C
options.text: The reaction proceeds through a free carbocation that rotates 180° before capture.

options.label: D
options.text: trans-2-Butene isomerizes to cis-2-butene during the reaction.

questions.correct_answer: Bromine forms a symmetrical bridged bromonium ion; subsequent backside attack by bromide at either carbon occurs with equal probability to produce identical meso enantiomeric faces.
questions.explanation: Bridged halonium formation followed by anti-stereospecific backside attack on trans-2-butene yields the symmetric (2R,3S)-meso-2,3-dibromobutane.

questions.question: What reactive intermediate enforces the syn stereochemistry in OsO₄ dihydroxylation of alkenes?

options.label: A
options.text: An open carbocation intermediate that is captured by hydroxide from water.

options.label: B
options.text: A free radical intermediate with a long lifetime.

options.label: C
options.text: An epoxide intermediate that undergoes double inversion.

options.label: D
options.text: A cyclic five-membered osmate ester intermediate formed by concerted [3+2] cycloaddition to one face of the alkene double bond.

questions.correct_answer: A cyclic five-membered osmate ester intermediate formed by concerted [3+2] cycloaddition to one face of the alkene double bond.
questions.explanation: Both oxygen atoms are tethered to the same osmium atom and delivered simultaneously to the same face of the alkene in a concerted step.

questions.question: In the enantioselective reduction of ketones by the (R)-CBS catalyst, how is facial selectivity achieved?

options.label: A
options.text: The catalyst acts as an achiral solvent that increases reaction temperature.

options.label: B
options.text: The reaction proceeds via an SN1 ionization of the carbonyl oxygen.

options.label: C
options.text: The chiral oxazaborolidine coordinates both the borane and the ketone, orienting the bulky group away from the catalyst to deliver hydride to the re-face.

options.label: D
options.text: The catalyst racemizes the product after reduction.

questions.correct_answer: The chiral oxazaborolidine coordinates both the borane and the ketone, orienting the bulky group away from the catalyst to deliver hydride to the re-face.
questions.explanation: Steric coordination in the well-defined CBS transition state differentiates between the enantiotopic faces of the prochiral ketone.

questions.question: What is the physical-chemical basis for resolving racemic acids with a pure chiral amine?

options.label: A
options.text: The resulting (R,R) and (S,R) ammonium carboxylate salts are diastereomers with different crystal lattice energies, solubilities, and melting points.

options.label: B
options.text: The chiral amine destroys one enantiomer by chemical oxidation.

options.label: C
options.text: The amine inverts the stereochemistry of the (S) enantiomer to (R).

options.label: D
options.text: The salts become volatile and separate by gas distillation.

questions.correct_answer: The resulting (R,R) and (S,R) ammonium carboxylate salts are diastereomers with different crystal lattice energies, solubilities, and melting points.
questions.explanation: Diastereomeric salts have different physical properties, allowing clean fractional crystallization of one diastereomer.

questions.question: Why does rotating a Fischer projection by 180° in the plane of the paper maintain the identical stereochemical configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: It transforms the molecule into a constitutional isomer.

options.label: B
options.text: It reflects the molecule through an internal mirror plane.

options.label: C
options.text: A 180° rotation converts an (R) enantiomer into an (S) enantiomer.

options.label: D
options.text: A 180° planar rotation keeps horizontal bonds pointing forward and vertical bonds pointing back, preserving all CIP spatial relationships.

questions.correct_answer: A 180° planar rotation keeps horizontal bonds pointing forward and vertical bonds pointing back, preserving all CIP spatial relationships.
questions.explanation: A 180° in-plane rotation is a symmetry operation that does not invert stereocenters (unlike a 90° rotation, which inverts configuration).

questions.topic: Cis vs Trans Alkene Heat of Combustion
questions.question: Why does cis-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane have a higher heat of combustion than its trans isomer?

options.label: A
options.text: The cis isomer experiences steric repulsion (van der Waals strain) between the two eclipsing methyl groups on the same face of the ring.

options.label: B
options.text: The trans isomer contains more C-C single bonds.

options.label: C
options.text: The cis isomer has a higher molecular weight than the trans isomer.

options.label: D
options.text: The cis isomer is an antiaromatic molecule.

questions.correct_answer: The cis isomer experiences steric repulsion (van der Waals strain) between the two eclipsing methyl groups on the same face of the ring.
questions.explanation: Steric clash between cis substituents elevates ground-state potential energy, releasing more heat upon complete combustion.

questions.question: Why do enantiomers exhibit dramatically different biological and pharmacological effects?

options.label: A
options.text: Enantiomers have different chemical formulas in vivo.

options.label: B
options.text: One enantiomer is always radioactive.

options.label: C
options.text: Chiral biological receptors require a three-point spatial interaction that can only be matched by one specific enantiomer (like a right hand in a right glove).

options.label: D
options.text: Enantiomers have different boiling points in aqueous blood.

questions.correct_answer: Chiral biological receptors require a three-point spatial interaction that can only be matched by one specific enantiomer (like a right hand in a right glove).
questions.explanation: Biological enzymes and receptors are chiral polymers (proteins) that interact stereospecifically with asymmetric substrate topographies.

questions.question: Why is (2R,4S)-pentanediol achiral despite possessing two stereogenic carbon centers?

options.label: A
options.text: It possesses an internal plane of symmetry (σ) that reflects the (R) center into the (S) center, causing exact internal compensation of optical rotation.

options.label: B
options.text: The chiral centers have zero optical rotation individually.

options.label: C
options.text: It undergoes rapid interconversion with a planar enol isomer.

options.label: D
options.text: The two hydroxyl groups form an intramolecular covalent bond.

questions.correct_answer: It possesses an internal plane of symmetry (σ) that reflects the (R) center into the (S) center, causing exact internal compensation of optical rotation.
questions.explanation: Meso compounds possess an internal mirror plane or inversion center, making the molecule superimposable on its mirror image.

questions.question: Why does E2 elimination require an anti-periplanar transition state geometry?

options.label: A
options.text: The base must attack the leaving group directly from the front.

options.label: B
options.text: The C-H σ bonding orbital and the C-X σ* anti-bonding orbital must be parallel (dihedral angle 180°) for continuous orbital overlap as the new π bond forms.

options.label: C
options.text: It allows the leaving group to retain its stereochemical configuration.

options.label: D
options.text: A 180° angle minimizes the molecular weight of the transition state.

questions.correct_answer: The C-H σ bonding orbital and the C-X σ* anti-bonding orbital must be parallel (dihedral angle 180°) for continuous orbital overlap as the new π bond forms.
questions.explanation: Anti-periplanar geometry maximizes constructive overlap between the breaking C-H σ orbital and the forming π system, lowering the activation energy.

questions.question: Why does rotating a Fischer projection by 180° in the plane of the paper maintain the identical stereochemical configuration?

options.label: A
options.text: It reflects the molecule through an internal mirror plane.

options.label: B
options.text: A 180° planar rotation keeps horizontal bonds pointing forward and vertical bonds pointing back, preserving all CIP spatial relationships.

options.label: C
options.text: It transforms the molecule into a constitutional isomer.

options.label: D
options.text: A 180° rotation converts an (R) enantiomer into an (S) enantiomer.

questions.correct_answer: A 180° planar rotation keeps horizontal bonds pointing forward and vertical bonds pointing back, preserving all CIP spatial relationships.
questions.explanation: A 180° in-plane rotation is a symmetry operation that does not invert stereocenters (unlike a 90° rotation, which inverts configuration).

options.label: D

questions.explanation: Meso compounds possess an internal mirror plane or inversion center, making the molecule superimposable on its mirror image.

questions.question: Why does E2 elimination require an anti-periplanar transition state geometry?

options.label: A
options.text: The C-H σ bonding orbital and the C-X σ* anti-bonding orbital must be parallel (dihedral angle 180°) for continuous orbital overlap as the new π bond forms.

options.label: B
options.text: A 180° angle minimizes the molecular weight of the transition state.

options.label: C
options.text: It allows the leaving group to retain its stereochemical configuration.

options.label: D
options.text: The base must attack the leaving group directly from the front.

questions.correct_answer: The C-H σ bonding orbital and the C-X σ* anti-bonding orbital must be parallel (dihedral angle 180°) for continuous orbital overlap as the new π bond forms.
questions.explanation: Anti-periplanar geometry maximizes constructive overlap between the breaking C-H σ orbital and the forming π system, lowering the activation energy.

questions.question: What is the geometric and orbital structure of the transition state during an SN2 displacement on a chiral carbon?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: A planar carbocation with completely dissociated leaving group.

options.text: A trigonal bipyramidal arrangement where the central carbon is sp²-like, with the nucleophile and leaving group occupying axial positions at 180°.

questions.correct_answer: A trigonal bipyramidal arrangement where the central carbon is sp²-like, with the nucleophile and leaving group occupying axial positions at 180°.
questions.explanation: The nucleophile donates electron density into the σ* anti-bonding orbital directly opposite the leaving group, causing umbrella-like stereoinversion.

questions.question: Why does cis-1,2-dimethylcyclopropane have a higher heat of combustion than its trans isomer?

options.label: A
options.text: The cis isomer experiences steric repulsion (van der Waals strain) between the two eclipsing methyl groups on the same face of the ring.

options.label: B
options.text: The cis isomer has a higher molecular weight than the trans isomer.

options.label: C
options.text: The cis isomer is an antiaromatic molecule.

options.text: The trans isomer contains more C-C single bonds.

questions.correct_answer: The cis isomer experiences steric repulsion (van der Waals strain) between the two eclipsing methyl groups on the same face of the ring.
questions.explanation: Steric clash between cis substituents elevates ground-state potential energy, releasing more heat upon complete combustion.
